meta.description: Validate Kubernetes manifests against the real OpenAPI schema, catch deprecated apiVersions, and find YAML syntax errors — entirely in your browser, no upload.

heading: Kubernetes YAML Validator
tagline: Paste a Kubernetes manifest (or several, separated by ---) and check it against the real Kubernetes schema before you kubectl apply it.

ui.dropHint: Drop a .yaml/.yml file here, or paste manifest text above.
ui.privacyNote: Parsing and validation run in your browser. Only schema files are fetched from a public CDN: the resource schema and, for custom resources, the CRD catalog entry — requested by group/kind/version only, your manifest is never sent.
ui.multiDocHint: Multiple manifests separated by "---" are validated as separate documents.
ui.emptyState: Paste a Kubernetes manifest above (or load the sample) and the validation results will appear here.
ui.validationFailed: Validation failed unexpectedly. Try again or simplify the input.

issues.yaml-alias-limit: This document uses YAML aliases that expand too much to validate safely ({{message}}).
issues.empty-document: This document is empty — a manifest needs at least apiVersion and kind.
issues.empty-document-trailing: Empty document after the last "---" (harmless, but you can delete the trailing separator).
issues.not-a-mapping: A Kubernetes manifest must be a YAML mapping (key: value pairs) at the top level, not a list or a plain value.
issues.deprecated-api-version: "{{apiVersion}}" is deprecated for kind "{{kind}}" — use "{{suggested}}" instead.
issues.deprecated-ingress-backend: Changing only apiVersion is not enough for Ingress: networking.k8s.io/v1 also needs spec.rules[].http.paths[].pathType and backend.service.name/port instead of serviceName/servicePort. The "Copy with apiVersion fixed" button converts these too — review the result.
issues.unsupported-kind: "{{kind}}" is not one of the resource kinds this tool validates against a schema yet ({{supported}}). Syntax and deprecated-apiVersion checks still apply.
issues.schema-unavailable: Could not load the {{kind}} schema for Kubernetes {{version}} (network error or unavailable version) — schema validation was skipped for this document.
issues.schema-additional: {{path}}: unknown field "{{field}}" (not allowed by the schema)
issues.duplicate-key: Duplicate YAML key — a mapping key appears more than once (many tools silently keep only the last value).
issues.crd-validated: {{kind}} ({{apiVersion}}) was validated against the community CRD catalog schema (Datree), which may lag behind your operator version.
issues.xref-duplicate-name: {{kind}} "{{name}}" in namespace "{{namespace}}" is already defined in document {{first}}.
issues.xref-selector-template-mismatch: {{kind}}: spec.selector.matchLabels does not match spec.template.metadata.labels (not in the template: {{labels}}) — the API server rejects this.
issues.xref-service-no-match: Service "{{service}}": the selector ({{selector}}) does not match the labels of any workload in this file.
issues.xref-service-port-missing: Service "{{service}}" targets port {{port}} but no container of {{workloads}} declares it (containerPort or port name).

ui.optCrd: Look up custom resources (CRDs) in the community catalog (Datree)
ui.optSkipUnknown: Ignore kinds that have no schema (hide the "unsupported kind" warning)
ui.optCross: Cross-check resources (Service selector, ports, duplicate names)
ui.securityAllGood: No security findings for this workload.

checks.privileged: Container "{{container}}" runs privileged and has nearly full access to the host.
checks.allow-privilege-escalation-unset: Container "{{container}}" does not set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false (the default allows it).
checks.run-as-user-low: Container "{{container}}" runs as UID {{uid}}; a UID of 10000 or higher avoids clashes with host users.
checks.run-as-non-root: Container "{{container}}" is not forced to run as non-root (runAsNonRoot).
checks.read-only-root-fs: Container "{{container}}" has a writable root filesystem.
checks.cap-sys-admin: Container "{{container}}" adds the SYS_ADMIN capability (close to privileged).
checks.cap-drop-all: Container "{{container}}" does not drop ALL capabilities.
checks.host-network: The pod uses the host network namespace (hostNetwork).
checks.host-pid: The pod shares the host PID namespace (hostPID).
checks.host-ipc: The pod shares the host IPC namespace (hostIPC).
checks.host-path-socket: Volume "{{name}}" mounts the container runtime socket {{path}} — this is equivalent to root on the node.
checks.default-service-account: The pod uses the default service account.
checks.image-latest: Image "{{image}}" in "{{container}}" has no fixed tag or digest (or uses :latest).
checks.image-pull-policy: Container "{{container}}" uses a mutable image tag with imagePullPolicy: {{policy}}, so nodes can run stale images.

fixes.privileged: Remove privileged or set securityContext.privileged: false.
fixes.run-as-root: Set runAsUser to a non-zero UID and runAsNonRoot: true.
fixes.run-as-non-root: Add securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true (and a numeric runAsUser).
fixes.read-only-root-fs: Add securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and mount emptyDir volumes for writable paths.
fixes.cap-add-all: Remove ALL from capabilities.add and add only the specific capabilities you need.
fixes.cap-add: Keep capabilities.add as small as possible and review each one.
fixes.cap-drop-all: Add capabilities.drop: ["ALL"] and add back only what is required.
fixes.host-network: Remove hostNetwork or set it to false.
fixes.host-pid: Remove hostPID or set it to false.
fixes.host-ipc: Remove hostIPC or set it to false.
fixes.host-path-socket: Do not mount the runtime socket; use a dedicated build service or rootless tooling.
fixes.host-path: Prefer emptyDir, a PersistentVolumeClaim or a ConfigMap/Secret volume.
fixes.default-service-account: Create a dedicated ServiceAccount with the minimum RBAC and set serviceAccountName.
fixes.image-latest: Pin the image to a specific version tag or a sha256 digest.
fixes.image-pull-policy: Pin the image tag, or set imagePullPolicy: Always.
fixes.liveness-probe: Add a livenessProbe so Kubernetes restarts stuck containers.
fixes.readiness-probe: Add a readinessProbe so traffic only reaches ready pods.
fixes.seccomp-profile: Add securityContext.seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault (pod or container level).

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: No. `kubectl apply --dry-run=server` is the only check that runs against your actual cluster's API server (including any CRDs and admission webhooks it has installed), and `kubeconform`/`kubeval` are mature CLI tools built for CI pipelines. This validates the same class of things — YAML syntax, schema shape, deprecated apiVersions — from a browser tab, before you have `kubectl` configured against anything, or while reviewing a manifest someone else sent you.
faq.q2: Where do the schemas come from?
faq.a2: From `yannh/kubernetes-json-schema`, a community-maintained, automatically-updated mirror of Kubernetes's own OpenAPI-derived JSON Schemas, fetched on demand from a public CDN for the Kubernetes version you pick. Nothing about your manifest is sent anywhere — only the (versioned, public) schema file itself is downloaded, the same file for every user validating that kind/version.
faq.a3: Deployment, Service, Ingress, ConfigMap, Secret, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job, CronJob, and PersistentVolumeClaim cover the large majority of hand-written manifests. Other kinds still get full YAML syntax checking and deprecated-apiVersion detection — they just don't get schema-shape validation yet.
faq.q4: Does my YAML ever leave my browser?
faq.a4: No. Parsing and schema validation both run with plain JavaScript in this tab — the only network request this tool ever makes is fetching the public JSON Schema file for the resource kind and Kubernetes version you selected, never your manifest content.

article.heading: Catching Kubernetes manifest mistakes before kubectl does
article.p1: A rejected `kubectl apply` is usually the first time a mistake in a Kubernetes manifest becomes visible — and by then you're often mid-deploy, staring at an error message that quotes a JSON Schema validation path (`spec.template.spec.containers[0].image: Required value`) that doesn't obviously map back to the YAML file you were just editing. Catching the same class of error earlier, with the exact line highlighted, turns that into a five-second fix instead of a context switch.
article.p2: YAML's own syntax has sharp edges that don't show up in most other config formats: indentation is significant and inconsistent tabs/spaces will silently produce a different (wrong) structure rather than an error in some cases, `---` document separators are easy to lose track of in a long multi-resource file, and a stray extra level of nesting reads as valid YAML while meaning something completely different to Kubernetes. This tool parses with the same library approach that keeps full source position information through parsing, so a syntax problem is reported against the real line it occurs on, not just "somewhere in this 200-line file."
article.p3: Deprecated apiVersions are a slower-motion trap: `extensions/v1beta1` Deployments, `apps/v1beta1`/`apps/v1beta2` StatefulSets and DaemonSets, and `networking.k8s.io/v1beta1` Ingresses all still parse as perfectly valid YAML and even worked on older clusters — until the cluster gets upgraded past the version where Kubernetes finally removes the old API group entirely, at which point every manifest using it starts failing to apply with no warning beforehand. Catching these while editing (with the exact replacement apiVersion suggested) avoids finding out during a cluster upgrade instead.
article.p4: Schema validation against the real Kubernetes OpenAPI spec catches the rest: a `replicas` field that ended up as a quoted string instead of a number, a `containerPort` outside the valid range, a required field like `spec.selector` on a Deployment that got deleted while copy-pasting between manifests. None of these are YAML syntax errors — the file parses fine — which is exactly why a dedicated schema pass catches what a quick visual read of the file usually doesn't.
